# Study A — whole-program authority verification at scale

*Generated by `delulu-measure study-a`. Raw data: `results.json`. Method and threats to validity: `METHODOLOGY.md`.*

## Corpus

5 chains, 25 packages, minimum dependency depth 4.

| Chain | Shaped like | Packages | Depth | Lock (ms) | Verify (ms) | Clean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cliwc` | CLI tool | 5 | 4 | 18 | 21 | yes |
| `parsecfg` | parser | 5 | 4 | 15 | 21 | yes |
| `httpstack` | HTTP client stack | 5 | 4 | 14 | 19 | yes |
| `sitegen` | static site generator | 5 | 4 | 17 | 19 | yes |
| `agenttool` | agent-tool server | 5 | 4 | 14 | 18 | yes |

## The injection campaign

An effect was injected at **every library position in every chain** — 20 sites. Each injection adds an effect, declares it honestly in the victim's own manifest, and ships it as a PATCH version bump, which is what a real supply-chain attack looks like: not a package lying about itself, but one being truthful about a change nobody reads.

**Caught: 20 of 20 (100.0%).**

Every mutation was checked to COMPILE on its own before its result was recorded (20 of 20 valid). This fence matters: an earlier version of this study injected code that did not parse, and scored a clean 100% that the authority mechanism had not earned — the builds were failing on syntax. An injection that does not compile is an experiment defect, not a catch.

### The negative control

The identical pipeline — fresh copy, lock, rebuild — run with **no mutation at all**, once per chain. Every one must build clean, otherwise the campaign is refusing regardless of what was injected and a 100% catch rate would mean nothing.

**5 of 5 controls built clean.**

The claim under test is a claim of *mechanism*, so the required rate is 100% and it is met — over valid mutations, against a control that proves the pipeline can decline to catch. A mechanism that caught 97% would have a hole to find, not a number to round.

### By depth

Depth 1 is a direct dependency; depth 4 is the leaf, four levels below the application — the position an attacker would prefer.

| Depth | Sites | Caught |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 | 5 |
| 2 | 5 | 5 |
| 3 | 5 | 5 |
| 4 | 5 | 5 |

## Time to verify

Verifying all 25 packages across 5 graphs took **98 ms** in total (19 ms mean per graph). These are wall-clock numbers from one machine and one run; they are reported as measured and are not a performance claim (see the stability contract: performance is measured, never promised).
